guidance_note: When the PR's own CHANGELOG names two callers that hand stored ranks to the same primitive (anchorRun and smoothRanks), apply the fix for a precondition gap to every named caller in the same commit, not only the one the reviewer pointed at.

evidence: The reviewer's trace holds: with order [a..f] and b depending on e, the stable sort yields [a,c,d,e,b,f], so b falls behind c and d which share no edge with it, contradicting "an issue changes place only when an edge pushes it past something"; 1af8edf narrowed the three comments and added a property assertion.
guidance_note: Before writing a guarantee about an algorithm into a doc comment or CHANGELOG, state it as a property and assert it in the existing property test; an overclaim that no test checks is the one a reviewer finds.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 1af8edf did not touch ranking.go, and the per-rewrite smoothing loop and its comment appear as original-PR lines in the hunk. guidance_note: When adding a loop that calls a side-effecting helper once per item, add a test that pushes several items through the helper's trigger condition in one call before the reviewer asks for it.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 7b6d5c3 did not touch rank.go, and "That is the failure arm, and it is the whole of it" was original-PR text. The function also fails on negative n and on lower >= upper, so the sentence overclaimed; a32005e listed all three failure modes.

The agent deleted the early return so the doc holds for every n, rather than qualifying the doc. That is safe because spacedRanks still returns nil,nil for n == 0 after validating, and a test covers it.
guidance_note: When rewriting a doc to enumerate a function's failure modes, read the function's early returns top to bottom and check each listed failure is reachable for every input class, including the n == 0 fast path.

narrative: The PR replaced the rank-inversion repair with a stable topological sort plus an LIS of anchors. Most findings across five reviewed rounds were overclaiming doc comments: order preservation, minimality, 'only shortens', 'leaves alone', the error surface. The reviewer surfaced these piecemeal, and most were present in the original PR, so the ON-NAMED-FIX flags are largely false positives. The real fix-caused costs are the F1 guard applied to anchorRun but not smoothing (F12), comment drift from the Significant switch (F3) and from the F6 doc rewrite (F14), a missed sibling overclaim in the paragraph F2 edited (F7), and doc duplication from the F9 restructure (F13). Every round-4 finding was fix-caused, so that round was avoidable; round 5 hit the review cap and was not reviewed.
guidance_observations: Before the first push, check every guarantee sentence in doc comments and the CHANGELOG against a counterexample or a property test; this PR spent four rounds trimming overclaims one at a time.
When a fix closes a precondition gap on a shared primitive, list every caller (the CHANGELOG already named both) and close or rule out each before replying 'Fixed'.

When a reply to one finding states a fact (smoothing cannot shorten, smoothing rewrites any rank), grep for comments asserting the opposite and fix them in the same push. F10 and F11 sat beside statements the agent had just made.
The final fix commit e7cf98f landed after the MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS cap, so the head merged unreviewed. Fix-caused rounds use up the review budget the merge gate depends on.
